subject: Proposal: 24–36mo Commitment Options & Deployment Ramp (Sage Analytics)

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Nov 2025 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Initial pricing options for multi-year commitment

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I pulled together two clean options for a 24–36 month commitment that align with the throughput profile you shared (steady ramp to 2M tokens/day by month 9). The intent is to give Sage a predictable unit cost while keeping headroom for burst usage.

Attached: Sage_24-36mo_Term_Comparison.xlsx (spreadsheet) — high-level discounts, quarterly ramp schedule, and per-token rates by model family. Also included a draft Ramp_Schedule PDF.

High level:
- 24-month: 12% discount on published hosted rates; accelerated billing (quarterly invoice).
- 36-month: 18% discount on published hosted rates; annual prepay preferred for the best economics.
- Both options include a 6-month onboarding credit (100K tokens/month) and one free migration window.

Questions for you:
1) Would procurement prefer annual-in-advance prepay, or are quarterly invoices with committed minimums acceptable?
2) Do we need a carve-out for dev/non-prod usage (we can exclude from committed buckets and bill at metered rates)?

If these look directionally right, I can loop in finance for an approval and a signable term sheet.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the XLS. Elena and I reviewed with finance this morning. A few follow-ups:

- The 36-month option looks attractive, but our CFO is asking whether Redwood can offer a stepped discount that increases if we hit defined usage thresholds (i.e., 18% baseline, +2% at 24 months if usage >= 80% of committed).
- Procurement prefers annual-in-advance prepay for capex planning, but we need more flexible ramp credits in year 1 — our ramp may be faster in Q1.
- Can you confirm whether non-prod usage can be excluded from the committed buckets? That’s important for our dev teams.

Can you put a proposal together that includes: stepped discount schedule by milestone, an annual prepay option with a partial refund clause tied to underutilization, and explicit non-prod carve-out? If possible, include a sample invoice schedule.

Looking forward —
Tom
Head of Platform Engineering
Sage Analytics
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Sage — stepped discount & prepay ask (need approval)

Marissa, Karthik —

Forwarding Tom's note. Sage wants:
1) 36-month baseline at 18% with a +2% uplift if usage thresholds are met at 24 months;
2) annual prepay is preferred, but they want a partial refund clause if they underutilize (<70% after year 1);
3) carve-out for non-prod/dev. They also want an invoice schedule sample and confirmation about how credits apply during a faster ramp.

Proposed quick approach:
- Offer two signable term variants: Annual-prepay (best rate) or Annual-invoiced-with-committed-minimums. In either case, we give a 12-week lookback step that can trigger the +2% discount at the 24-month mark.
- Refund policy: pro-rated credit toward future usage or a limited refund (capped) if utilization < 50% after year 1. Finance will want this tightly scoped.
- Non-prod: exclude from committed bucket if teams label projects and send usage tags — we can gate by token tag.

Karthik — need quick confirmation on two things:
A) Can Finance approve an effective max refund liability of up to 15% of year-one prepay if utilization falls below the agreed threshold?
B) Operationally, can we support token tagging to exclude non-prod consumption from committed tiers?

If approved, I'll draft the term_sheet_SIGNABLE.pdf and send to Tom/Procurement.

Rishi
